title: Manager Coach: Hazira gas terminal release and fire, 2020
status: Learning purposes: not a statutory document. Draft learnings from a ProbeMatrix investigation export; validate them before adoption.

data_quality.text: Draft learnings from an unreviewed analysis: the export's Investigation Status is in_progress and no finding is marked as edited by a person, so this pack stays a draft until the investigation is completed and reviewed.

exclusions.reason: Left out of the Learnings Register after a reviewer downgrade vote; the vote is recorded in the register's source note, not in this export. Left out here for the same reason.

bottom_line.text: Several controls existed only on paper: a change procedure not used since 2018, an emergency plan without isolation criteria, and audits that recorded compliance without data.
No function owned the specification for a legacy pressure seal, so a substitute part became regular practice.
No procedure required a design-pressure test before pressure-boundary work went back into service.
Records held the warnings (repeat seal changes, wall loss, an open notification), but no system turned them into a decision.
Emergency isolation depended on reaching hand-operated valves inside the release area.

items.lesson: Emergency isolation depended on reaching valves that could only be closed by hand inside the release area.
items.explanation: The gas terminal isolation valves had no remote operation from the control room. When the vapour cloud denied access, the first isolation came only after a senior role reached the gate and the valve could be closed by hand. The operating system assumed access would be possible.

items.lesson: Once the cloud blocked access, the shift response stayed on locating the leak rather than switching to upstream isolation.
items.explanation: Nothing in the plan or at the console told the shift when to stop searching and isolate from a distance. Each report went up the chain while people tried to approach the source on foot in very poor visibility.

items.lesson: Control-room staff held emergency duties without a defined qualification.
items.explanation: New and transferred staff received a four-day general course and then on-the-job training; no qualification was defined in the HR or operations policy and there was no simulator practice. The rostering system had nothing to check against.

items.text: With Mechanical Maintenance (the largest interface, 71 shared findings): agree that operations accepts a pressure-boundary job back into service only against a signed test record; the meter went back online after an operating-pressure soak [FND-FD617187; FND-611A8BFC; EVD-2894; EVD-0185].

With Emergency Planning & Command: agree the isolation criteria, the valve list and the shift roles that may isolate without calling up the chain, and drill them together [FND-314D34C5; FND-AE629313; EVD-4052; EVD-3932].

items.change: Convert the gas terminal emergency isolation valves to remotely operated valves, operable from the control room and a safe secondary location.
items.indicator: Share of identified emergency isolation points with remote operation; proof-test pass rate.

items.change: Provide control-room isolation matrices for major releases, showing which valves isolate each section and where each can be operated from.
items.indicator: Isolation matrices in place for every hydrocarbon area and used in drills.
items.why_not_stronger: The decision aid is the system fix for the switch from locating to isolating; the engineering fix (remote isolation) is the recommendation above, and the matrix is needed to use it.

lint_ok.reason: the administrative change is itself the system fix here, as why_not_stronger explains

items.change: Define a control-room operator qualification with simulator-based emergency scenarios and a pass standard, and make it a rostering prerequisite.
items.indicator: Share of control-room positions on each shift filled by qualified staff.
items.why_not_stronger: Competence is the condition here; the rostering prerequisite turns training into a check the system enforces, and the engineering isolation fixes are recommended separately.

lint_ok.reason: the administrative change is itself the system fix here, as why_not_stronger explains

items.name: Time to isolation in drills
items.measure: Time from a confirmed release to first isolation in each drill; baseline from the next two drills
items.deterioration: Any drill where isolation waits for someone to reach a valve in the release area

items.name: Qualified control-room cover
items.measure: Share of shifts with every control-room position filled by a qualified person, from the roster and training records
items.deterioration: Any shift rostered without a qualified person in the control room

rows: Confirm which isolation valves are local-only and which control-room staff hold no defined qualification; brief each shift on isolating from a distance
Draft the isolation matrices and the qualification with control-room operators and shift in-charges
Report time to isolation in drills and qualified cover in the monthly operations report

items.lesson: A pressure-boundary seal was replaced with an unspecified local part because no one held the specification.
items.explanation: The 1986 meter's original gasket specification was not on file, so locally bought O-rings were fitted as regular practice, with no specification or quality check at purchase and no recorded decision to switch. The job had to be done, and the export shows nothing in the system that said stop.

items.lesson: Pressure-boundary work went back into service without a test to design pressure, because no procedure required one.
items.explanation: After the gasket change on 18 September 2020 the system was pressurised to operating pressure only, and the meter was taken online the next day. No procedure set a test type, pressure or witness for these high-pressure meters.

items.lesson: Repeat failures of the same seal were treated as routine repairs, not as a reliability warning.
items.explanation: The gasket was changed in November 2018, February 2019 and September 2020. Each job closed as a repair; no repeat-failure review existed to open a root-cause investigation.

items.lesson: A high-consequence repair depended on one person's judgement, with no independent check of part, method or test.
items.explanation: The gasket job was planned with no inspection, test-witness or close-out role and without a job safety analysis, so the substitute part and the missing test reached service unchecked.

items.text: With Work Management & Planning: agree that pressure-boundary jobs are planned as safety-critical, with test and witness steps written into the job plan [FND-F8C125D5; EVD-5105].

With Engineering, Design, Documents & MOC: agree who re-establishes a lost specification and who approves a substitute part, and that a substitute triggers a change review [FND-A2048FB8; FND-5A5F6AB3; EVD-8645; EVD-2986].

items.change: Configure the work-order system so a pressure-boundary job cannot be closed, or the equipment released to operations, until a test result is entered.
items.indicator: Attempted closures blocked for missing test data, trending to zero.

items.change: Set an automatic repeat-failure trigger in the maintenance system that opens a root-cause investigation task for a repeat corrective job on the same item.
items.indicator: Bad actors flagged per quarter and the share with a completed root-cause analysis.

items.change: Re-establish the seal design for the meter flange (OEM data or an engineered equivalent), stock only certified parts against it and quarantine non-conforming seals.
items.indicator: Share of critical pressure-boundary spares with a specification and certificate on file.

items.name: Pressure-boundary jobs with a test record
items.measure: Share of pressure-boundary work orders closed with a recorded test result and witness; baseline from a sample of current work orders
items.deterioration: Any pressure-boundary job closed without a test result

items.name: Repeat failures reviewed
items.measure: Share of repeat corrective jobs on the same item that opened a root-cause review
items.deterioration: A repeat failure closed as a routine repair

rows: List pressure-boundary items with no specification on file and every repeat-failure item; hold any substitute seal for engineering approval
Draft the return-to-service procedure and the work-order block with the fitters and supervisors who do the work
Report test-record share and repeat failures reviewed in the monthly maintenance report

items.lesson: The management-of-change procedure existed on paper but had not been used since 2018.
items.explanation: The procedure was published in August 2016, yet no change went through it after 2018, including the switch from the original gasket to a local O-ring. The export shows no prompt in the work or stores systems that treats a like-for-unlike part as a change.

items.lesson: The metering P&ID was a lost original replaced by an unapproved vendor drawing that did not match the field.
items.explanation: Old drawings were lost and a vendor drew new ones, which were never approved and did not match the valves and meters on site. Maintainers had no verified reference for the gasket job.

items.text: With Mechanical Maintenance and Materials Management: agree that a non-catalogue or substitute part cannot be issued without a change reference, and who in engineering approves it [FND-5A5F6AB3; FND-8083ECAC; EVD-2986; EVD-8645].
With Operations & Control Room: agree which safety-critical drawings operations relies on in an emergency, so those are field-verified first [FND-583EB5FE; EVD-0933].

items.change: Build a change trigger into the work-order and stores issue screens, so a non-catalogue or substitute part needs a management-of-change reference.
items.indicator: MOC records raised per month, and the share of substitute-part issues with an MOC reference.

items.change: Field-verify and re-issue controlled P&IDs for the gas terminal, starting with metering and emergency isolation systems.
items.why_not_stronger: Drawing control is itself the system fix for lost and unapproved drawings; no engineering control replaces a verified drawing.

lint_ok.reason: the administrative change is itself the system fix here, as why_not_stronger explains

items.name: Change control in use
items.measure: MOC records opened and closed per month; baseline from the records since 2018
items.deterioration: A month with no MOC records while field changes are made

items.name: Verified safety-critical drawings
items.measure: Share of safety-critical P&IDs field-verified and approved
items.deterioration: Any vendor drawing in use without approval

rows: Confirm which changes since 2018 had no MOC record and which safety-critical drawings are unapproved
Draft the change trigger and the 'replacement not in kind' examples with maintenance, stores and operations
Report MOC activity and drawings verified in the monthly engineering report

items.lesson: Known pipe-wall loss was measured but not acted on: no corrective plan for three years, and painting used as the fix.
items.explanation: The 2017 thickness survey found pipes needing corrective action, and three years later there was no plan. A July 2019 spot check found 1.03 mm of wall loss with heavy pitting on the 36-inch line, and painting was the corrective action. Measuring was in place; deciding was not.

items.lesson: The four-year thickness inspection cycle slipped to six years, and baseline data and pipe schedules were missing.
items.explanation: The last two surveys were in 2011 and 2017, and for many gas terminal pipes the baseline thickness and original drawings were not available. The schedule had no escalation when it slipped.

items.text: With Mechanical Maintenance: agree that every wall-loss finding gets a repair, re-rate or replace decision before any painting closes it [FND-47B1702F; FND-5EC15274; EVD-2397].
With Operations & Control Room: agree how overdue integrity actions on lines in service are reported to the shift and to site leadership [FND-6D307E93; EVD-5527].

items.change: Carry out fitness-for-service assessments on the 2017 and 2019 wall-loss locations, then repair, re-rate or replace as required.
items.indicator: Open wall-loss findings without a fitness-for-service decision, trending to zero.

items.change: Schedule thickness inspections in the maintenance system with automatic escalation when overdue, and use the 2011 data as the baseline where originals are lost.
items.indicator: Inspections done on time against the plan.
items.why_not_stronger: Scheduling with automatic escalation is the system fix for a slipped inspection cycle; the engineering fix for the measured wall loss is the fitness-for-service recommendation above.

lint_ok.reason: the administrative change is itself the system fix here, as why_not_stronger explains

items.name: Wall-loss findings without a decision
items.measure: Count and age of wall-loss findings with no fitness-for-service decision; baseline from the 2017 and 2019 findings
items.deterioration: Any finding older than one inspection cycle without a decision

items.name: Inspections on time
items.measure: Share of scheduled thickness inspections done in their interval

rows: List every open wall-loss finding and every overdue inspection; confirm the 36-inch segment's condition
Draft the integrity action register and the escalation rule with the inspectors and maintenance planners
Report overdue integrity actions and inspection compliance in the monthly report to site leadership

items.lesson: Safety audits used generic checklists and recorded compliance without site data, so they could not find plant-specific defects.
items.explanation: The self-safety audit checklist was not related to the specific plant and recorded compliance where the data was later found incomplete; internal audits kept no filled checklists. The audit method could not have found the seal, test or isolation gaps.

items.lesson: Maintenance notifications were treated as work permits, permits went missing untracked, and job safety plans were absent.
items.explanation: Some work permits were missing with no tracking, and job safety plans were not attached in the work system, so hazardous maintenance went ahead without a documented hazard analysis.

items.lesson: Fire drill records held no actions or observations, so drills could not show whether readiness was improving.
items.explanation: Drill reports in the work system held dates only, and a separate record was not in line with the approved guidelines.

items.text: With Mechanical Maintenance: agree that work opening a hydrocarbon pressure boundary needs its own permit and job safety analysis, separate from the maintenance notification [FND-7E1F2B3F; EVD-5105].
With Emergency Planning & Command: agree one drill record with timings for detection, notification and isolation, so drills test the isolation decision [FND-B8B75D91; EVD-2130].

items.change: Make the electronic permit mandatory for hydrocarbon work with an attached job safety analysis, and reconcile issued against closed permits daily.
items.indicator: Unreconciled permits per week, trending to zero; share of permits with a job safety analysis attached.

items.change: Replace generic checklists with site-specific, barrier-based audit protocols that need evidence (a photo, record or reading) for each compliance claim.
items.indicator: Share of audit items with recorded evidence; plant-specific defects found per audit.
items.why_not_stronger: The audit method is the condition; an evidence requirement is the system fix for audit quality, and no engineering control audits a plant.

lint_ok.reason: the administrative change is itself the system fix here, as why_not_stronger explains

items.name: Audit claims with evidence
items.measure: Share of audit compliance claims with recorded evidence; baseline from the last self-safety audit
items.deterioration: Any audit recording compliance without evidence

items.name: Permits reconciled
items.measure: Issued permits not matched to a closed permit at the end of each week

rows: Re-test a sample of last year's 'compliant' audit items and reconcile current permits
Draft the plant-specific audit protocol and the permit reconciliation with the auditors and permit issuers
Report audit evidence share and permit reconciliation in the monthly HSE report

items.lesson: The malfunction notification was never closed or reviewed, so the last administrative check before return to service did not happen.
items.explanation: A notification for the meter was raised on 17 September 2020 and was not closed after the gasket job; no one was assigned to review the closure.

items.lesson: Pressure-boundary work was planned like any other repair, without inspection, witness or job safety steps.
items.explanation: The gasket job plan had no independent check, test witness or job safety analysis, so the planning system did not put a verification step between the fitter and the restart.

items.lesson: Repeat failures were planned as routine repairs: the same seal was replaced three times in 22 months, and each time the planning system scheduled another like-for-like job with no trigger for a reliability review.
items.explanation: No rule in the work-management system escalated a second or third corrective job on the same tag to root-cause analysis, OEM seal restoration or meter replacement, so the inadequate repair was planned again until the fourth failure.

items.lesson: Planned inspection slipped without a deferral decision: the four-year thickness survey ran in 2011 and 2017 only, and the next one was already overdue by 2020.
items.explanation: The schedule let a mandated inspection move by years with no recorded deferral, approval or risk assessment, so the slip was invisible to the people who could have resourced it.

items.change: Link equipment status to notification status in the maintenance system, so equipment cannot be set available while its corrective notification is open.
items.indicator: In-service equipment with an open corrective notification, by age.

items.change: Introduce a safety-critical maintenance category in work planning that adds inspection, test-witness and close-out review steps automatically.
items.indicator: Share of safety-critical jobs with every verification step signed by someone other than the performer.

items.change: Add a repeat-failure trigger to the maintenance system: a second corrective job on the same tag within 24 months opens a reliability review that must be closed before the next job on that tag is scheduled.
items.barrier: prevention: reliability review of repeat failures
items.indicator: Tags with two or more corrective jobs in 24 months and no closed reliability review.

items.change: Schedule mandated inspections as fixed-interval work orders that cannot be moved without a deferral record: the reason, a risk assessment and the approval of the integrity function's manager.
items.why_not_stronger: Deferral control is a management-system rule; the stronger fix for known wall loss, repair or fitness-for-service assessment, belongs to asset integrity (LR-17) and is in that function's section.
items.indicator: Mandated inspections past their due interval, and deferrals without an approved record.

lint_ok.reason: Deferral control is a management-system barrier; its tier is stated honestly, and the stronger fix for the wall loss itself is in the asset-integrity section.

gaps.text: [GAP] The export does not show the functions' own backlog, deferral or resourcing data for the period before the event.
gaps.evidence_needed: Maintenance and inspection backlog reports, deferral records and staffing levels by function for 2018 to 2020.

limits: Function sections cover the five functions with the most T3 findings; F11 and F13 tie at 55 findings and F11 is written out because F13 (plant leadership) is served by site-leadership-coach.
A management-review input table is not included; add it when the coach feeds a management review.
The analysis is a desk review of the published enquiry report; it had no site access or interviews.
